title: Cascade routing (FrugalGPT)
change: Opt-in PASTURE_CASCADE: answer local, escalate to cloud only on low confidence
reason: Committing to a route up front wastes cloud spend on prompts the local model could handle
effect: Verified: cascade never runs for sensitive content or streaming; cloud failure falls back to local. Tested with mock backends.
grounding: ADR-011; FrugalGPT arXiv:2305.05176

title: Data-driven threshold calibration
change: calibrate command recommends PASTURE_THRESHOLD from the user's own PII-free token-size log
reason: The strongest routers are learned from labels a single local user does not have; calibrate the one length knob from real usage instead
effect: Advisory threshold derived from the (1-target) quantile of logged prompt sizes; stays deterministic and offline
grounding: ADR-023, ADR-015; RouterBench arXiv:2403.12031, UCCI arXiv:2605.18796

title: Privacy-classification routing
change: std-only classifier forces sensitive prompts local, overriding even --cloud
reason: A privacy-first proxy's worst failure is leaking PII to the cloud
effect: Sensitive content kept on-device unless PASTURE_ALLOW_SENSITIVE_CLOUD; only category labels logged, never values
grounding: ADR-007; PRISM arXiv:2511.22788

title: Richer difficulty features
change: Hard-signal step adds reasoning-depth, strict-format, math-density, multi-question markers (EN+JA)
reason: Token length alone under-routes genuinely hard short prompts
effect: More hard prompts escalate to the stronger model; local-only setups unaffected; still deterministic and label-only
grounding: ADR-008; routing survey arXiv:2506.06579

title: Evaluation harness
change: eval runs a labelled set (correctness) + threshold sweep (cost/locality)
reason: Routing quality must be measured, not asserted, to answer the brittle-rules critique
effect: Accuracy, cloud rate, false/missed escalations reported; fully offline regression gate
grounding: ADR-012; RouterBench arXiv:2403.12031

title: Exact-match response cache
change: Opt-in PASTURE_CACHE keyed by hash(model+messages), bounded FIFO
reason: Repeated identical prompts should not re-pay the backend
effect: Hits skip the backend (cost 0, route=cache); sensitive prompts never cached; composes with cascade
grounding: ADR-013; GPTCache

title: SSE streaming
change: Proxy detects stream:true and streams chat.completion.chunk frames for all backends
reason: OpenAI clients expect token-by-token streaming
effect: Local NDJSON/SSE re-emitted over the std-only socket; privacy/routing decide before the first byte; cascade stays non-streaming by design

title: API-surface parity: /v1/models + /v1/embeddings
change: Added GET /v1/models and POST /v1/embeddings (local-only) to the proxy
reason: Many OpenAI clients probe /v1/models on connect and 404 hid the server; embeddings clients (LlamaIndex/LangChain) need the endpoint
effect: Clients connect cleanly; embeddings routed to the local backend only; OpenAI-shaped responses; unit-tested
grounding: ADR-030, ADR-034; COMPETITIVE.md peer-surface gap

title: Cloud retry + local fallback
change: Classify 5xx as retryable Transport; complete_with_retry with exponential backoff (PASTURE_CLOUD_RETRY), then fall back to local
reason: A single transient cloud error should not fail the request or silently degrade
effect: Transient failures retried then fall back to local when available; 4xx not retried; tested with a flaky mock (no sleeps)
grounding: ADR-032; LiteLLM/Portkey failover

title: Tool/function-calling as a hard signal
change: parse_request detects non-empty tools/functions; decide_full escalates to cloud
reason: Tool use is most reliable on the stronger model; unparsed tool calls were misroutable to a weak local model
effect: Tool requests escalate (gated by code_to_cloud, overridden by privacy); fields passed through unchanged; 4 tests
grounding: ADR-031

title: GPU-less / local-only PC enhancement
change: PASTURE_LOCAL_ONLY (force local), PASTURE_LOCAL_FAST_MODEL (dual-local routing), PASTURE_INJECT_CONTEXT (date/OS system message); CPU-only model tier in `models`
reason: No-GPU and air-gapped machines should run a capable local assistant with zero cloud dependency
effect: All traffic stays on-device when enabled; simple short prompts use a tiny fast model; lightweight models gain date/OS grounding; std-only
grounding: ADR-035; two-tier local cascade (RESEARCH.md cat.1/cat.8)

title: PII detection hardening (7 to 10 categories)
change: Added pem_key, url_credential, env_secret detectors; expanded EN/JA keywords and vendor key prefixes
reason: PEM private keys, DB URLs with credentials, and .env secret pastes were not caught and could leak to the cloud
effect: Three new leakage vectors detected before they leave the machine; labels only, never values; 26 new tests
grounding: ADR-036; over-classification bias (false positive=local=cheap, false negative=leak)

title: Self-improvement ledger
change: Machine-readable IMPROVEMENTS.jsonl (change/reason/effect/status/grounding) + `pasture improvements` + a CI-checked validator
reason: The improvement history was human prose scattered across three docs; the durable asset is a verified, queryable improvement record, not the model
effect: Every shipped change is now a structured, self-verifying causal record; the bundled ledger is validated by a compile-time test
grounding: ADR-037; RSI=Search*Verification*Compression — this is the Compression/asset layer

title: Optional semantic cache
change: Cosine-similarity cache via the local /v1/embeddings (off by default)
reason: Exact-match caching misses paraphrases; embeddings can catch them without a new crate
effect: Not yet implemented; would stay opt-in to preserve the zero-dependency default
grounding: COMPETITIVE.md IMP-12; GPTCache, arXiv:2603.03301

title: Calibrated-uncertainty escalation (UCCI-style)
change: Map local mean-logprob to an estimated error probability (isotonic, std-only)
reason: Turns the escalation knob from a target-rate into a target-accuracy budget
effect: Not yet implemented; honest about single-user label scarcity
grounding: COMPETITIVE.md IMP-13; UCCI arXiv:2605.18796

title: Bearer-token auth + rate-limit
change: Optional PASTURE_AUTH_TOKEN (Bearer required on /v1/*, constant-time compare) and PASTURE_RATE_LIMIT (global token bucket, req/min); /health exempt; warn when bound non-localhost without auth
reason: The proxy is localhost-only by default but users expose it (PASTURE_LISTEN_ADDR=0.0.0.0); network exposure needs an auth + flood gate
effect: Gated via check_gate before route dispatch; 401/429 with OpenAI envelope; std-only token bucket tested deterministically (no sleeps); 12 tests; off by default so the zero-config single-user path is unchanged
grounding: ADR-040; COMPETITIVE.md IMP-15; LiteLLM/Portkey auth

title: Live metrics endpoint
change: GET /v1/stats returns JSON aggregates (route counts, rates, tokens, spend) over the cost-log counters
reason: A live observability view should not require parsing JSONL by hand; stats was CLI-only
effect: Read-only PII-free endpoint reusing cost::summarize; missing log reads as zeros; 4 tests (shape, empty, counted, roundtrip)
grounding: ADR-038, COMPETITIVE.md IMP-16; LiteLLM/Portkey dashboards

title: Sampling-parameter passthrough
change: parse_request extracts temperature/top_p/max_tokens/stop/seed/presence_penalty/frequency_penalty into SamplingParams; each backend serializes them (OpenAI fields, Ollama options/num_predict, Anthropic max_tokens+stop_sequences); cache key includes them
reason: Peers (LiteLLM/OpenRouter/Ollama/LM Studio/vLLM) honor these; Pasture silently dropped them, so temperature:0 determinism and max_tokens cost caps were ignored — a correctness gap
effect: Client sampling intent now reaches the backend; cache no longer serves a temperature:0 answer to a temperature:1 request; non-finite values rejected at parse; 11 tests across parse/build/cache
grounding: ADR-039; OpenAI Chat Completions API; peer-gateway parity

title: CORS / OPTIONS preflight for browser clients
change: Opt-in PASTURE_CORS_ORIGINS (comma list or *): OPTIONS preflight answered with 204 + Access-Control-Allow-* (before auth), and Access-Control-Allow-Origin reflected on all responses incl. SSE; specific origins add Vary: Origin
reason: Browser UIs (Open WebUI web, custom dashboards) cannot call the proxy without CORS preflight handling — peers (Ollama/LM Studio/LiteLLM) all support it
effect: Browser clients can connect when enabled; off by default since a localhost server with * CORS is reachable by any visited website; deterministic, std-only; 8 tests (parse/match/headers/preflight/roundtrip)
grounding: ADR-041; Ollama OLLAMA_ORIGINS, LM Studio/LiteLLM CORS

title: Streaming token usage (stream_options.include_usage)
change: When the client sets stream_options.include_usage, the SSE stream emits a final chunk with empty choices and a usage object (prompt/completion/total_tokens) before [DONE]
reason: OpenAI/LiteLLM/vLLM emit usage on the stream when asked; Pasture's streaming path reported no token counts, so clients tracking cost/length on streamed responses got nothing
effect: Streamed responses now carry usage when requested; off unless the client opts in (no extra bytes otherwise); std-only; 4 tests (parse/build/roundtrip with and without)
grounding: ADR-042; OpenAI Chat Completions streaming usage

title: Structured-output (response_format / JSON mode) passthrough
change: parse_request captures response_format; forwarded verbatim to OpenAI/OpenAI-compat and translated for Ollama (json_object -> format:json, json_schema -> the schema in top-level format); cache key includes it. Added a JsonValue serializer (to_json_string) to round-trip arbitrary values
reason: OpenAI/vLLM/LM Studio/Ollama all support JSON mode / structured outputs; Pasture silently dropped response_format, so JSON-mode requests returned free-form text
effect: JSON-mode and json_schema requests now reach the backend; deterministic BTreeMap-ordered serializer reused for hashing; 9 tests (serializer round-trip, per-backend emission, parse, cache)
grounding: ADR-043; OpenAI response_format, Ollama format

title: Unique completion ids (chatcmpl-...)
change: Responses now carry a unique id (chatcmpl-<clock><counter>) instead of the constant "pasture"; streaming chunks share one id per stream (id threaded through build_openai_chunk / build_openai_usage_chunk)
reason: OpenAI returns a unique id per completion that logging/observability/dedup tooling keys on; a constant id breaks tracing and de-duplication
effect: Buffered responses get a fresh id each; all chunks of one stream share it; uniqueness via an atomic counter; std-only; 2 new tests (uniqueness, stream id-consistency) + builder call-site updates
grounding: ADR-044; OpenAI chat.completion id

title: GET /v1/models/{id} (single model retrieve)
change: Added the OpenAI models.retrieve endpoint: /v1/models/{id} returns the model object when id is configured, else 404; the bare /v1/models list path is unaffected
reason: OpenAI SDK and some client validation flows call models.retrieve(id); Pasture only served the list, so retrieve fell through to the list via starts_with
effect: Single-model GET returns OpenAI {id,object:model,owned_by} or a 404 envelope; query string and trailing slash tolerated; 5 tests
grounding: ADR-045; OpenAI Models API

title: Per-connection socket read/write timeout (slow-loris guard)
change: serve sets a per-connection read+write timeout (PASTURE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT, default 30s); read_request maps a timed-out read to a 408 response instead of pinning the worker; 0 disables
reason: read_request had no timeout, so a slow/dead client could hold a bounded worker thread forever and a handful could exhaust the pool (slow-loris DoS)
effect: Slow clients are dropped with 408 after the window, freeing the worker; std-only TcpStream timeouts; 408 added to the status table; 3 tests incl. a fast 50ms timeout roundtrip
grounding: ADR-046; continuation of IMP-21 DoS hardening (body/header/recursion caps)

title: system_fingerprint on responses and stream chunks
change: All buffered chat responses and SSE chunks now carry system_fingerprint: fp_pasture_XXXXXXXX (FNV-1a of model name, truncated to 32 bits); all chunks of one stream share the fingerprint computed at stream start
reason: OpenAI clients key caching-invalidation, dedup, and model-change detection on system_fingerprint; Pasture omitted it entirely, breaking those clients
effect: Deterministic, model-keyed fingerprint on every response and chunk; same-stream consistency; std-only FNV hash, no I/O; 4 tests
grounding: ADR-047; OpenAI Chat Completions API system_fingerprint

title: model field in streaming chunks
change: build_openai_chunk and build_openai_usage_chunk now carry a model field; the streaming path passes req.model computed once at stream start
reason: OpenAI includes model in every chat.completion.chunk; clients logging or displaying per-chunk model received nothing
effect: All SSE chunks carry model; same-stream consistency; std-only; 3 tests
grounding: ADR-048; OpenAI Chat Completions streaming API

title: logprobs:null in choice objects
change: build_openai_response and build_openai_chunk now emit logprobs:null in each choice object (usage chunk unaffected, empty choices)
reason: OpenAI always includes a logprobs key in each choice; strict client schema validators could reject Pasture responses that omitted it
effect: Buffered and streaming choices carry logprobs:null, completing choice-object parity; purely additive, std-only; 2 tests
grounding: ADR-049; OpenAI Chat Completions choice object

title: HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connection reuse
change: handle_connection loops (cap 100) serving sequential requests on one TCP connection; per-connection conn_buf carries read-ahead bytes across iterations; write_response gains keep_alive:bool for Connection header; HTTP/1.1 defaults to keep-alive, HTTP/1.0 to close, SSE always closes
reason: Re-connecting for every request adds one TCP round-trip of latency; OpenAI clients and proxies expect persistent connections for batch workloads
effect: Clients reuse connections; read-ahead bytes preserved correctly via drain; existing timeout/body-cap/rate-limit guards apply per-request; std-only; 4 tests
grounding: ADR-050; HTTP/1.1 RFC 7230 §6.3; LiteLLM/OpenRouter persistent connection behaviour

title: HEAD /health and /v1/engines alias
change: HEAD /health accepted (correct Content-Length, no body, RFC 7231); /v1/engines[/{id}] aliased to /v1/models in dispatch; write_head_response helper
reason: Monitoring tools use HEAD for liveness probes; old OpenAI SDK versions and some clients probe /v1/engines for model discovery
effect: HEAD liveness checks work; old SDK clients discover models without 404; purely additive, std-only; 3 tests
grounding: ADR-051; RFC 7231 §4.3.2; OpenAI engines API (deprecated)

title: X-Request-ID echo
change: read_request parses X-Request-ID header (CRLF-injection guard strips \r\n from value); handle_connection echoes it back on every response via extra header block; SSE responses also carry the echoed header; absent when client omits the header
reason: Clients correlate asynchronous responses and trace distributed calls by request ID; without echo the ID is invisible to the caller
effect: All response types (buffered, streaming, error, HEAD) echo the caller-supplied ID; CRLF injection guarded; purely additive, std-only; 3 tests
grounding: ADR-052; OpenAI API X-Request-ID convention; LiteLLM request-id passthrough

title: 405 Method Not Allowed for known routes
change: route_allowed_methods maps known paths to their allowed methods; dispatch catch-all returns 405 + Allow header when the path is known but the method is wrong, 404 only for unknown paths
reason: HTTP/1.1 RFC 7231 §6.5.5 requires 405 with an Allow header when the method is not supported; returning 404 for wrong methods misleads clients and debuggers
effect: GET /v1/chat/completions → 405 Allow: POST,OPTIONS; DELETE /v1/models → 405; /no/such → 404; purely additive, std-only; 3 tests
grounding: ADR-053; RFC 7231 §6.5.5; LiteLLM/OpenRouter correct method handling

title: tool_choice as a hard escalation signal
change: parse_request also sets has_tools=true when tool_choice is present and not "none" (covers auto/required/named-function values)
reason: Some clients send tool_choice without a tools array, or send tool_choice:required which is stronger than auto; both are unambiguous intents to call a tool
effect: tool_choice:auto/required/named-function all escalate to the stronger model; tool_choice:none does not; combines with existing tools/functions detection; 4 tests
grounding: ADR-054; OpenAI tool_choice parameter spec; SPEC.md §3.1 deferred item

title: POST /v1/completions legacy text-completion shim
change: parse_legacy_completion maps prompt (string or string array) to a single user message; handle_legacy_completion routes through run_completion and formats the result as object:text_completion with choices[].text; id prefix cmpl- matches OpenAI convention; 405 for wrong method; streaming not supported via this shim
reason: Many older LLM clients, SDKs, and tools (LM Studio, older langchain/openai-python) default to /v1/completions; returning 404 breaks those clients silently
effect: Old-style text-completion clients work without reconfiguration; prompts are routed through the same privacy/routing/cache pipeline; std-only, 6 tests
grounding: ADR-055; OpenAI text completions API (deprecated but widely used); LiteLLM completions compat

title: Configurable system prompt via PASTURE_SYSTEM_PROMPT
change: system_prompt: Option<String> field on Proxy; with_system_prompt builder; prepend_system_prompt helper merges with existing system messages; applied first in run_completion (before inject_context); PASTURE_SYSTEM_PROMPT env var and system_prompt config-file key; empty string treated as None
reason: Single-user PC assistant use case requires a persistent persona/instruction prompt (e.g. "You are a coding assistant") without rebuilding inject_context; complementary to date/OS injection
effect: All requests get the configured system prompt prepended; existing system messages in the request are merged (configured prompt first); std-only, zero-dep; 4 tests
grounding: ADR-056; LiteLLM system_prompt global override; Ollama modelfile system parameter

title: Live cache hit/miss counters in /v1/stats
change: AtomicU64 hits/misses added to ResponseCache; get() increments on hit or miss; hits()/misses() accessors; handle_stats reads live counters from self.cache; build_stats_response gains cache_hits/cache_misses params; 2 new fields in JSON response
reason: The existing cache_rate metric derives from the cost log (written only after completion); live counters show real-time effectiveness independent of log state, enabling tuning without log parsing
effect: GET /v1/stats now reports live cache_hits and cache_misses counts; std-only (AtomicU64); 2 new cache.rs tests + 1 stats integration test
grounding: ADR-057; Prometheus-style counters pattern; LiteLLM cache hit stats

title: 415 Unsupported Media Type for non-JSON POST bodies
change: read_request parses Content-Type header (lowercased); handle_connection checks it for POST requests before dispatch; returns 415 when Content-Type is present and does not start with application/json; absent Content-Type accepted (bare curl compatibility)
reason: Clients sending form-encoded or text bodies get a descriptive 415 instead of a confusing 400 JSON parse error; absent Content-Type accepted for simple HTTP clients
effect: Wrong Content-Type on POST → 415 with message; missing Content-Type → unchanged; charset suffixes accepted; std-only; 3 tests
grounding: ADR-058; RFC 7231 §6.5.13; OpenAI API Content-Type requirement

title: Model-pinned routing via req.model field
change: classify_and_decide checks req.model against configured local/cloud model names and the sentinels "local"/"cloud"; matching routes are forced via decide_full(forced=Some(Route)); with_model_names builder; wired in cli.rs from config.local_model/cloud_model
reason: Clients that are model-aware (e.g. specify model:gpt-4o-mini) expect to reach the cloud backend; without pinning they could be routed local on short prompts even when they explicitly requested a cloud model
effect: model:"local" / model:"<local_model_name>" → forced Local; model:"cloud" / model:"<cloud_model_name>" → forced Cloud (still subject to privacy override); unrecognised model names use normal routing; 5 tests
grounding: ADR-059; LiteLLM model routing; OpenRouter model-specific routing

title: Reject n > 1 with 400 Bad Request
change: parse_request checks the n field; if n != 1 (present and > 1 or zero), returns ProxyError::BadRequest with a clear message; n=1 and absent n both pass
reason: Without validation Pasture silently returns 1 completion when n>1 was requested, violating the contract; a clear 400 with explanation is always better than silent truncation
effect: Clients requesting n>1 get an immediate 400 with 'n must be 1' message; n=1 and absent n unchanged; 3 tests
grounding: ADR-060; OpenAI completions n parameter spec

title: POST /v1/moderations stub
change: handle_moderations parses input; build_moderations_response returns all categories false/0 in OpenAI moderation format; dispatch arm + 405 for wrong method
reason: Many OpenAI SDK versions call /v1/moderations unconditionally before or after completions; returning 404 breaks those clients silently
effect: Moderation clients receive a well-formed all-safe response and continue; Pasture does not run real content moderation (stub is explicit); std-only; 2 tests
grounding: ADR-061; OpenAI Moderations API; LiteLLM moderation passthrough

title: cache_size and cache_capacity in /v1/stats
change: ResponseCache gains cap() accessor; handle_stats reads len()+cap() from the cache; build_stats_response gains cache_size/cache_capacity params; both added to the JSON response
reason: Operators need to know whether the cache is near capacity to tune PASTURE_CACHE; the hit rate alone is insufficient for sizing decisions
effect: GET /v1/stats now includes cache_size (current entries) and cache_capacity (max entries); 0 when cache is disabled; std-only; 2 tests
grounding: ADR-062; Prometheus gauge naming conventions

title: Prometheus /metrics endpoint
change: build_metrics_response emits Prometheus text format v0.0.4 for all routing counters, cache stats, and token/cost gauges; handle_metrics reads the cost log + live cache state; write_plain_response sends text/plain; version=0.0.4; /metrics added to route_allowed_methods and dispatch; ADR-063
reason: Operators need a live pull-based metrics endpoint compatible with Prometheus/Grafana without parsing JSONL logs; /v1/stats is human-readable JSON but not scrape-compatible
effect: GET /metrics returns HELP/TYPE headers and labelled counters (route=local/cloud/cache) plus token/cost/cache gauges; wrong method returns 405; std-only; 3 tests
grounding: ADR-063; Prometheus exposition format v0.0.4; LiteLLM /metrics; Portkey observability

title: X-Response-Time header on every response
change: handle_connection captures Instant::now() after request parsing; te() closure appends X-Response-Time: <N>ms header to every write_response/write_plain_response/write_head_response/write_sse_headers call; covers success, error, and SSE paths (SSE reflects time-to-first-byte)
reason: Operators and SDK clients need per-request latency without parsing JSONL logs; X-Response-Time is a de-facto standard header used by nginx, Fastly, and Heroku
effect: Every HTTP response now carries X-Response-Time: <N>ms; std-only (std::time::Instant); backward-compatible (additive header); 3 tests
grounding: ADR-064; nginx X-Response-Time; Fastly / Heroku latency header conventions

title: Version field in /health response + 501 stubs for /v1/audio and /v1/images
change: /health response now includes version (compile-time CARGO_PKG_VERSION via concat!/env!); 501 Not Implemented returned for POST /v1/audio/* and /v1/images/* with not_supported error type; route_allowed_methods covers these paths so wrong-method returns 405 not 404; 501 and 405/415 added to status reason table in write_response
reason: Clients detect mismatched Pasture versions via /health; 404 for audio/images endpoints misleads SDK clients that probe them unconditionally — 501 correctly signals recognised-but-unsupported
effect: /health body includes version:"0.26.0"; audio/images return 501; wrong method still returns 405; status reason table more complete; std-only; 4 tests
grounding: ADR-065; OpenAI SDK multi-endpoint probing; nginx/LiteLLM health check version convention

title: Structured per-request access log (JSONL, no PII)
change: access_log: Option<String> field on Proxy; with_access_log builder; append_access_log writes one JSONL line per request (ts/method/path/status/ms/request_id?) before each response via access_log! macro; wr!/wrp!/wrh! macros unify response-writing in handle_connection; PASTURE_ACCESS_LOG env var + access_log config key; wired in cli.rs
reason: Operators need per-request visibility (latency, status, path) without parsing JSONL cost logs or scraping /metrics; access logs are the standard observability primitive
effect: PASTURE_ACCESS_LOG=/path enables append-only JSONL with ts/method/path/status/ms and optional request_id; no prompt content, no auth tokens, no PII; off by default; std-only; 4 tests
grounding: ADR-066; nginx/LiteLLM/Portkey access log conventions; OpenTelemetry access-log semantic conventions

title: TTL (time-to-live) eviction for the response cache
change: ResponseCache stores (CompletionResponse, Instant) pairs; get() changed to &mut self to lazily evict expired entries (removes from map, counts as miss); with_max_age builder + set_max_age mutating method; with_cache_ttl Proxy builder; PASTURE_CACHE_TTL env var (seconds, 0=disabled) + cache_ttl_secs config key; wired in cli.rs
reason: Without TTL, stale cached responses (outdated facts, old code, revoked context) are served indefinitely; long-running proxy processes need time-bounded cache entries for correctness
effect: PASTURE_CACHE_TTL=3600 makes entries expire after 1 hour; expired entries removed on first get after expiry; len() stays accurate; off by default (0=no TTL); std-only; 4 cache tests
grounding: ADR-067; Redis TTL semantics; GPTCache TTL; Nginx proxy_cache_valid
